items.title: Byron Stripling interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, April 25, 1998 [interview 1 of 2]
items.q: Play “Flight of the Bumblebee” or “Virgin dela Macarena” or something, some Rafael Mendez stuff.

ctx.x: Well maybe you played on it.

Maybe I did. I hope I’m getting paid for it. What do you need to be a Broadway musician? Okay? And then you write next to it what skills you need. A studio musician. What do you need to be a soloist in a jazz club? What do you need to be a classical soloist? Sometimes I’ll get a call to play with a concert band, to play just a classical oriented program, light classics. Play “Flight of the Bumblebee” or “Virgin dela Macarena” or something, some Rafael Mendez stuff. What are the skills? What do you need to do? And…
something, I want to fall into something, and what I want to fall into is the things I want to do. I want to have the trumpet mouthpiece up to my lips, because I love that.
